To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured two-particle correlations of a proton in the forward direction with a particle in the pionsation region.
the two-particle correlations of a pionization particle with a fragmentation proton are large and rise at small x of the fragmentation particle.
the correlation function is an energy-independent and rapidity-independent function of x of the proton in the fragmentation direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of two-particle correlation functions in proton-proton collisions at 200 GeV/c.
the production of particles with high transverse momenta in hadron-hadron collisions.
the correlation between the pion and proton in the fragmentation and pionization regions in the same event.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the correlation is a function of x only and is independent of the rapidity and energy of the proton.
the data are consistent with a picture in which the proton is formed by a coherent process in which all the constituents of the projectile proton interact with the target.
the correlation is independent of the x of the fragmentation particle, rises with x of the pion, and is independent of the rapidity and energy of the pionizing particle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have measured the correlation of the fragmentation proton with the pionization particles and have found it to be an energy-independent function.
the correlation between the pion production and the proton fragmentation is small and independent of energy and x.
the correlation between the pion and proton in this kinematical region is not due to a single mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the correlation between the fragmentation region and the pionization is not a function of the rapidity gap between these two regions.
the correlation between the pionisation region and the fragmentation is not an energy-independent function, as it was thought before.
the proton-proton correlation function for one particle in the fragmentation region is a function of x and that the correlation function is independent on x for x ⪅ x of the fragmentation particle.
